title: Provisioning lanes for air-gapped upgrade exemptions and risk forms
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We regularly receive enterprise requests for private/VPC/on-prem deployments that are explicitly air-gapped or require temporary network exemptions for upgrades. Current intake paths are ad-hoc, require repeated engineering SRE hand-holding, and lack a fast lane for low-risk exemptions. This causes long lead times and inconsistent customer experience.

Goal: Create a formal "Provisioning Lanes" playbook and associated intake artifacts (forms, scoring rubric, templated comms, and preflight checklists) that let Solutions Engineering and PMs: 1) Quickly triage whether a request can be handled via an automated low-touch provisioning lane (approved exemptions with guardrails), 2) Surface required artifacts up-front so engineering work is scoped correctly, and 3) Provide an auditable risk form and escalation path for requests that require manual review.

Scope: Non-bug customer requests only (new private/VPC/on-prem onboarding, upgrade windows, temporary bridge proxies for image pull, and one-off network allowances). Excludes ongoing runtime reliability incidents and security vulnerability patches.

Deliverables:
- Intake form template (self-serve + SE-assisted) capturing network diagram, upgrade window, allowed hosts, signing keys/KMS notes, airgap manifest, and owner contacts.
- Automated scoring rubric that produces one of three lanes: "green" (provisioning lane: approved with template + automated check), "amber" (requires SRE gating + scheduled maintenance window), "red" (manual security/engineering review).
- Risk exemption PDF template for customer signature and internal audit record.
- Preflight checklist and lightweight probe library (sample scripts) that SEs can run to validate firewall rules and proxy configs prior to scheduling.
- Templated comms and SLA commitments per lane (expected lead time, rollback requirements, and contact list).
- Playbook doc that maps who signs off at each lane, escalation rules, and a minimal list of deliverables for the engineering handoff.

Trade-offs considered:
- Automating scoring reduces time-to-onboard but risks missing nuanced infra constraints. To mitigate we add mandatory file uploads (network diagram) and an "SE confirm" step for green lane activation for new customers.
- Requiring signed risk exemptions increases legal friction; we'll gate this to amber/red lanes only.

Key stakeholders: Solutions Engineering (SE), Onboarding PMs, SRE, Security Compliance, Legal, and Dedicated/Private eng leads.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form prototype available in Confluence and as a Google Form linked from the onboarding portal
Automated scoring rubric implemented as a Google Sheets logic + documented rules in the playbook
Three lane definitions documented with SLAs and template comms for each lane
Probe scripts (basic TCP/HTTPS pull checks) committed to infra repo and linked from playbook
Risk exemption template reviewed by Legal and Security and stored in Drive
Pilot: 3 customers successfully processed via the green provisioning lane with <10% SE time spent per request
